## 1. Identity, scope and origin

**FICTIONAL throughout.** Record DEMO-DEC-01; concern DEMO-CON-01; action DEMO-ACT-01; control DEMO-CTL-01. This newly invented office-workflow example is not an actual Cedar Estuary event or a real user test. Origin: ORR-FRM-GEN-001 r01 and ORR-REG-GEN-001 r01. Events below use sequence labels, not actual timestamps. Personas are fictional roles, not actual appointments.

Objective: approved procedures have usable current forms. Risk: a procedure is revised while its form still requests obsolete information. Control: document owner reviews affected forms at each procedure change; the release custodian holds distribution until the review is recorded. Evidence: change-impact list and version-specific review decision.

## 2. Simulated entries and decisions

| DEMO-E01 | Reporter | An obsolete field is found; concern recorded | Process owner acknowledges and assesses |

| DEMO-E03 | Document owner | New review step and form revision recorded; requests closure | Reviewer receives implementation evidence |
| DEMO-E04 | Reviewer | No completed-use outcome evidence supplied; implementation alone insufficient | Chair retains DEMO-ACT-01 as outcome_pending; owner supplies scoped outcome evidence before renewed closure decision |

## 3. Current disposition and sign-off

Current action status: outcome_pending. No actual signatures, review competence, measurement or operating effectiveness exist. The invented chair has authority only in this example; the example does not authorize organizational action. Proposed next review is triggered by receipt of relevant outcome evidence, with escalation timing set by actual adoption, not this story.

## 4. Corrections and history

Preserve DEMO-E01–04; a later correction must reference the earlier event and record prior/new value, actor, reason and date. No correction or retrospective real observation is fabricated. r01: original fictional teaching record. Retain this public example; real records remain private under adopted controls.
